title: The robot upgrade
summary: Combine a printed part, a measured circuit and a mechanism into one real improvement to the mBot, then prove it with a fair before-and-after test.
materials: the season's electronics and mechanism parts
black electrical tape and poster board, for a fixed test course
the Maker's Log, open to weeks 1 to 10

steps.title: Ask, imagine, plan
steps.body:
The design loop, close to the season's end: ask, imagine, plan, build, test, fix.

Ask: can everything built this sprint combine into one real improvement, not three separate demos? A printed part, a measured circuit and a mechanism can work together on the same robot.

Imagine one upgrade that uses at least two of the three. It could be a printed bumper wired to an LED warning circuit that lights when it flexes, or a geared arm that clears an obstacle. It could also be a printed mount holding a sensor at a better angle found by testing.

Plan: pick one upgrade and sketch it. Design a fixed test course the mBot can run before the upgrade and after it, changing nothing else about the course or the robot's starting position between runs.

figure.alt: Three before-upgrade results cluster tightly together near the bottom, showing the normal wobble from run to run. Three after-upgrade results cluster higher up. The real question is whether the gap between the two clusters is bigger than the wobble within each one.

steps.title: Test it or trust it
steps.body:
It is easy to feel like a change made something better without actually checking. A part looks sturdier, a sensor seems steadier, and the feeling gets trusted instead of tested.

A before-and-after test replaces the feeling with a number. Run the same course the same way before the upgrade, several times, and write down what happens each time. Even an unmodified robot's runs wobble a little from run to run. Then make exactly one change, the upgrade, and run the same course the same way again, the same number of times.

Only then compare. The after numbers might be only a little better than the before numbers, close to how much the before runs wobbled among themselves. If so, the upgrade might not have done much at all. If the after numbers are clearly better than that wobble, the upgrade earned its claim. Feelings are a fine reason to try something. Numbers are the only fair reason to believe it worked.

figure.alt: A fixed test course runs from a marked start to a marked finish with tape marking both ends. The mBot, fitted with the upgrade, runs the same course each time, with the starting position and course kept identical between the before and after runs.

steps.title: Build the upgrade, then test before and after
steps.body:
Finish building the upgrade and check it is securely fitted before any testing begins. Set up the fixed test course with tape and poster board, and decide exactly what is being measured, time to finish the course or distance covered in a set time. Keep the same choice for every run.

Run the course three times with the mBot as it was before the upgrade, using the same battery charge level and the same starting position each time. Write down the three results.

Then fit the upgrade, changing nothing else about the robot or the course, and run the same course three more times the same way. Write down these three results next to the before ones.
checklist: The upgrade combines at least two of a printed part, a measured circuit and a mechanism
The test course, the starting position and what is measured stayed identical before and after
Three before runs and three after runs were completed and recorded
The upgrade is securely fitted and the robot completed every run without falling apart

steps.title: Before versus after
steps.body:
The course, the starting position and what is measured stay exactly the same for every row. Only whether the upgrade is fitted changes.

Six rows, three before and three after. For each row, write which condition it was, before or after, and the result, either time in seconds or distance in centimetres, whichever was chosen.
steps.question: Was the after result better than the before result by more than the wobble between the three before runs?

steps.title: Bug diary
steps.body: One line for each thing that did not work the first time and what you tried. Classics this week: a battery that ran down between the before runs and the after runs, making the comparison unfair. Also watch for a starting position that drifted slightly from run to run, which can look like the upgrade's doing when it is really just a wobble in setup.

steps.title: Show it
steps.prompt: Photo of the finished upgrade fitted to the mBot, plus your table of all six before-and-after results
